subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which default policy and implementation sequence should OpenClaw use to reduce model-facing tool-schema overhead without breaking cross-channel cron/isolated agents, provider schema contracts, or plugin/declarative tools?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the remaining work changes core prompt/schema defaults and crosses provider, channel, cron, Tool Search, plugin API, and compatibility boundaries that need maintainer sequencing.

options.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and land measured, compatibility-preserving reductions in prompt text, send-only schemas, Tool Search defaults, and deferred plugin/tool APIs.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Issues
options.body: Close or pause the umbrella only if maintainers decide the open narrower issues should own all remaining schema and prompt reductions independently.

options.title: Adopt Aggressive Lazy Defaults
options.body: Make lazy or slim schemas the default sooner, accepting higher compatibility and provider-contract risk for faster context reduction.

recommendation.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and land measured, compatibility-preserving reductions in prompt text, send-only schemas, Tool Search defaults, and deferred plugin/tool APIs.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest current history across the prompt/runtime/cron surfaces and participated in maintainer sequencing discussion.
